Revised assessment incorporating the October 2017 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS): The FOMC statement is growth-positive but inflation-cautious, with an accommodative stance and gradualism appropriate given below-target inflation and hurricane noise. However, SLOOS points to a more mixed credit backdrop than the statement alone implies: banks eased standards for C&I loans (a positive for business credit), but tightened terms for credit card and auto loans and reported weaker demand across several categories, including consumer credit and business purposes such as inventory, accounts receivable, plant/equipment investment, and M&A. Reasons cited for tightening included the economic outlook, portfolio quality, and risk tolerance, though competition supported some easing and banks maintained willingness to make consumer installment loans. Net, the strong labor market and solid activity are tempered by softer loan demand and tighter consumer credit terms, nudging the tone slightly less positive than before.
